title: Does the capture-kit packing result survive real, sourced device weights, energies and runtimes?
summary: Re-runs the capture-kit search (11,520 kits, 6,912 legal) on a catalogue of real devices whose weights, battery energies and runtimes come from manufacturer and retailer pages read 2026-10-21 (Insta360 X4, DJI Osmo Action 4, iPhone 15 Pro Max, Sony a7C II with three lenses, Peak Design tripod, two Anker banks). With a 4 h recording floor, exact search reaches all 18 band × viewpoint shots at 4 kg (the assumed catalogue needed 5 kg) and a greedy packer stalls at 12, as before: the lens-needs-a-body complementarity survives real figures. Sweeping the figures no source gave (phone recording draw, selfie-pole, mini-tripod and mast masses, within ±30%) shows the ranking is robust (greedy is below exact in 77–99% of draws from 1.5 kg up) but the exact variety at a given budget is not: at 4 kg it falls from 18 to as low as 8, so the mount masses, which no source gave, matter more than any camera. Not sourced: those mass and draw figures, the iPhone recording draw (Apple publishes playback only), cell voltages used to turn mAh into Wh, and which bands each device covers.
lede: what does the capture-kit packing result look like with real, sourced devices (Insta360 X4, DJI Osmo Action 4, iPhone 15 Pro Max, Sony a7C II and lenses, Anker packs)? Exact search reaches all 18 shots at 4 kg, greedy stalls at 12; the unsourced mount masses move the exact figure by up to 10 shots.
